models.model_label: FX risk and tax-motivated outbound income shifting (Table 3, column 2)
models.sample_description: Firm-year observations for U.S. MNCs with an average foreign effective tax rate below the U.S. statutory rate (potential outbound income shifters), in the FXRisk sample. The FXRisk sample covers 1993–2017 and includes 5,432 firm-year observations from 980 unique firms; the regression column reports N=5,432.
models.method_details: The paper reports regression coefficient estimates and t-statistics but does not identify the estimator used for this equation.

dependent_variable.name: FROS
dependent_variable.definition: Five-year foreign return on sales: the sum of foreign pretax income over t−4 through t divided by the sum of foreign sales over the same period. The paper describes this as its income-shifting measure.
dependent_variable.formula: sum(foreign pretax income, t−4…t) / sum(foreign sales, t−4…t)

independent_variables.name: FXRisk
independent_variables.definition: Firm-level subsidiary-weighted currency-risk measure at t−4. It is the negative of the currency stability scores weighted by the share of the firm’s foreign affiliates using each currency; higher values indicate less stable foreign currencies and greater exchange-rate volatility. It is demeaned for the interaction specification.
independent_variables.formula: −Σ_c FXScore(c,t−4) × [affiliates using currency c / total foreign affiliates]; demeaned for this specification

models.equation_text: FROS_{i,t} = β0 + β1 FTR_{i,t} + β2 FXRisk_{i,t−4} + β3(FTR × FXRisk) + Σβ4n Controls + Σβ5k IND_{i,t} + Σβ6t YEAR_{i,t} + ε_{i,t}

fixed_effects.details: Industry and year indicator fixed effects are included. The selected table/equation does not further identify the industry classification.

standard_errors.details: Standard errors are clustered by firm.

evidence.quote: Standard errors are clustered by firm.

preprocessing.description: FTR and FXRisk are demeaned when they enter this interaction specification.
Continuous variables are winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles, except FTR, which is restricted to [−1,0].
